author: Chicago City Wire
title: Jan Schakowsky criticizes Trump policies affecting healthcare and environment
text:
U.S. Rep. Jan Schakowsky Representing the 9th District of Illinois | Official U.S. House headshot
U.S. Rep. Jan Schakowsky Representing the 9th District of Illinois | Official U.S. House headshot
Jan Schakowsky, a member of the U.S. Congress representing Illinois' 9th District, has expressed her concerns over recent policy actions by former President Donald Trump through a series of tweets. Schakowsky, who has been serving in Congress since 1999, replaced Sidney R. Yates and previously served in the Illinois House of Representatives and the Cook County Board of Commissioners.
On February 19, 2025, Schakowsky criticized Trump's apparent inconsistency regarding Medicaid funding. In her tweet, she stated: "Trump last night: No cuts to Medicaid Trump this morning: Supports House GOP's budget with over $880 billion in cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act." She further warned against what she perceives as misleading statements from Trump: "Don't be fooled by Trump's lies. He wants tax cuts for billionaires funded by cuts to the lifesaving programs that..."
The following day, on February 20, 2025, Schakowsky addressed Trump's decision to suspend funding for resettlement agencies, emphasizing its detrimental impact on families in her district. She highlighted the efforts of local organizations such as Refugee One: "Trump's order to suspend funding for resettlement agencies directly harms families in the 9th District. @Refugee_One works tirelessly to help individuals who have fled violence and war become independent and self-supporting members of our community."
Later that day, Schakowsky tweeted about environmental concerns related to Trump's directives involving the Army Corps and infrastructure projects like the Line 5 pipeline. She raised alarms about potential risks to Lake Michigan's ecosystem: "Trump is directing the Army Corps to greenlight projects like the Line 5 pipeline, allowing them to skip the permitting process despite the critical and proven danger it poses to Lake Michigan." She accused Trump of prioritizing corporate interests over environmental safety: "Trump would rather enrich Big Oil execs than protect our clean water source."
